title: Most children will stand on a stool to reach something by about 30 months
summary: CDC says most children, 75 percent or more, show simple problem-solving such as standing on a small stool to reach something, by 30 months.
body: Under thinking skills at 30 months, CDC lists simple problem-solving, and the example is standing on a small stool to reach something. The item is one of the things most children, 75 percent or more, do by that age. It is not a test score, and the page says these materials are not a substitute for a validated screening tool. Reaching from a stool is why a high shelf is not the same as a locked cupboard. The storage advice is on the poison cards. A child who does not do this yet is not labeled by the checklist.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Reviewed 16 May 2026. Milestone means most children (75 percent or more), not every child, and the page says the materials are not a screening tool.
